title: Control scaffold & quick experiments — scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick brain-dump for mapping likely controls to evidence sources and open questions. Not polished — notes to self and next steps.

High-level goals (context):
- Prep minimal set of controls for first SOC2 readiness checkpoint (target: Hosted API + Dedicated).
- Identify low-friction evidence we can collect today and owners for each piece.
- Flag blocking gaps that require infra/product changes.

Control scaffold (rough pairs):
1) Access management (SSO + RBAC)
   - Candidate control: SSO enforced for all prod console access; admin role review quarterly.
   - Evidence locations: Okta admin logs (admin console), GSuite group membership exports, IAM role definition PRs in infra repo.
   - Quick experiment: run export of current admin group and diff against last saved snapshot (make snapshot).
   - Owner: Maya (identity), add infra ticket if missing API access.

2) Change control / deployment approvals
   - Candidate control: PRs for model-serving infra require 2 reviewers + security checklist.
   - Evidence: GitHub PR history (protected branches), CODEOWNERS, merge checks.
   - Gap: we have some repos where branch protection isn't enforced (temp list in infra audit). Need to add automation to snapshot branch protection status.

3) Logging & monitoring (availability + detection)
   - Candidate control: central logging of infra events + 90d retention for security events.
   - Evidence: Splunk/Logflare queries, forwarding config in ops repo, retention policy screenshots.
   - Quick note: confirm where function/tool-calls logs land for Hosted API requests (are request-level logs padded with PII?).
   - Owner: Lena (observability).

4) Key management & secrets
   - Candidate control: KMS usage for all production secrets, automated rotation schedule documented.
   - Evidence: KMS key policy snapshots, runbook for rotation, CI config referencing secrets manager.
   - Open question: for Dedicated customers who bring own KMS, what is our evidence boundary? (We need an FAQ entry).

5) Data access classification / data flows
   - Candidate control: data classification table + mapping of where customer data may touch (hosted, dedicated, private).
   - Evidence: architecture diagram, S3 bucket policies, VPC peering configs, dataflow confluence page.
   - TODO: sketch minimal dataflow diagram specifically for embeddings + chat logs retention.

Signals & quick checks (things I can do this week):
- Pull Okta admin activity for the last 90 days and stash as evidence artifact. (Sahil -> Maya: need Okta API token w/ audit scope)
- Run a sample query for 'admin:password' secrets in repo (repo-scoped grep) and raise tickets for findings.
- Export list of protected branches across top 10 infra repos and save snapshot.
- Save screenshot of KMS key policy for primary prod key and annotate owner.

Evidence hygiene: ephemeral vs persistent
- Prefer artifacts that are reproducible: exports (CSV/JSON), PR links, CLI command outputs saved as files.
- Avoid screenshots as sole artifact unless accompanied by a CLI/export. Screenshots ok for UI-only settings but add script to reproduce.

Risk questions to surface in team sync:
- How do we define "production access" across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? Are on-prem customers in-scope for Redwood evidence?
- Where are unstructured logs (tooling, evaluation harness) stored and how long do they persist? Which ones contain model prompts or customer data?
- For model rollouts (canary/A-B), what manual gates exist and can we get an audit trail?
- Are there any service accounts with broad scopes that are not owned by a single person/team?

Control mapping draft (quick):
- CC: Access controls -> Okta groups, IAM policies, console ACLs.
- CC: Change management -> GitHub PRs, release notes, deploy tags.
- CC: System ops (monitoring) -> Alerts history, runbooks, on-call rota.

Questions / unknowns (to resolve):
- Need a list of repos that handle production key configurations (S3 buckets, KMS, provisioning). Where is canonical list?
- Who is the canonical owner for Dedicated onboarding config? (Trio: Solutions Eng, Infra, Customer Success)
- Are audit logs for Private deployments aggregated to our central observability? Probably not — note for evidence boundary.

Notes to self (brain-trim):
- Keep artifacts small & reproducible. Export CSVs into evidence folder: evidence/soc2/q1-2026/*.
- Build a tiny script that signs exports with date + sha so we can show immutability (or use GCS signed object metadata).
- Start a simple checklist in Confluence with links -> once checklist hits ~50% auto-collected, request readiness review.

Meeting prep for sync with Lena & Maya (Mar 11):
- Bring list of top-10 infra repos and status of branch protection.
- Ask Maya for Okta audit token or scheduled export.
- Ask Lena for a map of logging pipelines and cost/retention tradeoffs.

Open action items (who/what/eta):
- Sahil: create evidence folder and initial exports (Okta, branch-protection) — ETA 2026-03-12.
- Maya: confirm admin group membership snapshot + identify wildcard admin SAs — ETA 2026-03-10.
- Lena: export list of logging indices and retention windows; mark indices with customer data — ETA 2026-03-15.

Roughs & heuristics (internal):
- Minimum viable evidence per control = 2 independent artifacts (one human-readable, one machine-export).
- If artifact is ephemeral (UI-only), pair with a screenshot + CLI command showing how to reproduce.

Fragmented ideas (brainstorm):
- Could we leverage CI to auto-export branch protection and KMS policy snapshots nightly and store in evidence bucket? Low effort and strong signal.
- Create a "SOC2 quick checklist" button in console to generate a self-check report for Dedicated customers — helps Q/A and reduces custom evidence questions.

Final note: file this as 'working scratch' — iterate rapidly. Keep this doc as the place for micro-decisions and owner assignments; move stable copies into Confluence when they're ready.

-- sahil
